in_text_mentions: X−ray examination showed sclerotic appearance of the bones (Figure 2). Bowing of the radius, coxa valga, genu valgum, short distal phalanges with cone shaped epiphyses, a relatively small thoracic cage with irregular ribbon−like ribs and iliac flaring were also noted. Hypophyseal MRI was normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Plain radiograph showing generalized skeletal findings of Melnick-Needles Syndrome, including rib anomalies and spinal curvature, consistent with the case description. B: Radiograph showing lateral view of the upper limb demonstrating humeral cortical irregularity, a classic finding in MNS. C: Orthopaedic radiograph of the legs showing bilateral bowed long bones, a characteristic feature of Melnick-Needles Syndrome. D: Pelvic radiograph showing hypoplastic structures and coxa valga, indicating developmental dysplasia of the hip secondary to skeletal dysplasia. E: Spinal radiograph demonstrating generalized osseous abnormalities, including curvature and cortical thinning consistent with MNS presentation. F: Elbow radiograph showing curved ulna and radius, characteristic of long bone malformation in this skeletal dysplasia. G: Hand radiograph used for assessment, showing that bone age was chronologically appropriate, which...

in_text_mentions: typical for Melnick−Needles syndrome with exophthalmos, full cheeks, high forehead and micrognathia, malaligned teeth, mild genu valgum, narrow shoulders, and small chest wall with pectus carinatus (Figure 1). Her height was 103 cm (<3rd percentile; SDS:−2.6) and her we ight was 21 kg (25th percentile). She was prepubertal according to Tanner staging. She was reported to suffer from frequent severe upper respiratory tract infections. She had a hoarse voice. She was wearing glasses for myopia. Examination findings were otherwise normal.
